transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, your clinical conversational agent. I conducted your post-cataract surgery follow-up check, and I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your recovery. Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're eager to get back to gardening! According to our guidelines, you can start with light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, I would recommend waiting a bit longer, at least 2-3 weeks, before doing anything too strenuous. This will help your eyes heal properly. In the meantime, it's also a good idea to wear protective eyewear when gardening. Would you like to ask another question?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the advice! I'd also like to know when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start using your eye drops for dry eyes again as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. You don't need to wait for any specific time frame to start using them again. Just remember to use them as directed. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's really helpful, thank you. I'm very sensitive to bright light right now - is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have some sensitivity to bright light after cataract surgery. If it's mild, we recommend just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside. However, if it's significant or accompanied by redness and pain, we may need to assess it further. So, if you're concerned, it's always best to contact your care team for advice. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense. I have one more question: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay. So, it's a good idea to keep an eye on it, but if you're concerned, it's always best to contact your care team for advice. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's all for now. Thank you for answering all my questions, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! It was my pleasure to help. I'm glad I could answer all your questions. Before we go, can you confirm that all your questions have been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thank you once again!
